text:
dana: Quick note — new int8-tool-invoke build (raven-int8-v3) failing structured-output compliance more often in our smoke canary. Baseline fp16: ~0.1% parse failures; int8: ~0.9%. Most hits are small requests with kv-prefixes and batch size=1.

lee: ouch. can you paste a representative log?

sara: is this only func-calls or general json output?

dana: mostly func-calls (tool invocation objects). here's an excerpt from the canary job: 
```
2024-12-02T15:02:11Z request_id=cli-8372 model=raven-int8-v3 batch=1 kv_prefix_len=56 tokens=34 status=ok output=TRUNCATED parse_error=missing_trailing_brace
2024-12-02T15:02:11Z request_id=cli-8373 model=raven-int8-v3 batch=1 kv_prefix_len=10 tokens=6 status=ok output=EXTRA_COMMA parse_error=unexpected_token
```

dana: failures correlate with short completions (<= 30 tokens) and when prefix shares structural tokens (like '[' or '{').

raghav: did we change sampling/temp/prompt for int8 canary? quant only should affect logits but maybe decoding behavior shifted.

dana: same prompt, same top-p. quant config is micro-quant int8 with asymmetric clip; runtime flags: `--kv-cache=enabled --continuous-batching=on --max-batch=4` for the canary.

lee: two hypotheses: 1) timing/batching boundary produces truncated stream (stream cut off mid-json) 2) small numeric shifts change tokenization leading to subtle trailing chars. both could produce parse failures.

sara: quick repro: run local micro-canary with `--batch=1 --max-tokens=40 --prefix-mode=kv` and feed the failing prompt set. add `--stream-boundary-log=true` to capture boundary events.

ops-bot: deploy job queued: canary-int8-v3-2375 started (10k requests). progress: 23%

dana: telemetry snapshot: parse_fail_count=92 / 10000 for int8 (0.92%), baseline fp16 snapshot: 8 / 10000 (0.08%). Retry success rate when we do a single json-retry wrapper: ~60% of those 92 recover.

lee: that suggests recoverable truncation rather than catastrophic hallucination. any pattern on where the parse fails (start vs end)?

dana: mostly tail chop or stray comma. very rarely mismatched bracket.

raghav: immediate mitigations: increase retry budget for this canary from 1->3, enable a lightweight postprocess that attempts `jsonwrap` (wrap output with {"result": <raw> } then parse) and a streaming flush at end-of-sequence detection. we should also try canary with `--max-batch=1` and `--disable-continuous-batching`.

lee: agree. also add a validation gate that increments a metric `struct_fail_unrecovered` for failures not healed by retry+wrap. if that stays >0.2% we block promotion.

dana: running a quick AB: same 10k corpus, int8 with disable-batching = will start in 5m. ci-bot will post results.

ci-bot: ab-test started: int8-disable-batching vs int8-default. expected runtime ~18m.

(20m later)

ci-bot: ab-test finished. summary: int8-default: 92 parse fails (0.92%), int8-no-batching: 24 parse fails (0.24%), retry-recoverable proportion increased from 60% -> 78% when batching disabled.

dana: good signal — appears continuous batching is amplifying tail truncation for small outputs on this quant profile.

sara: next steps: 1) add small change to runtime to do an explicit stream-flush after final token for batch sizes that have short outputs 2) land jsonwrap fallback in postprocess 3) rerun quant calibration with more samples at short-length distribution

raghav: I'll open a ticket with links + telemetry + assign infra/srv. suggest we hold rollout until flush + wrap are in (or disable continuous-batching for int8 routes).

lee: +1. please include the minimal repro command and the sample failing request IDs in the ticket.

dana: creating ticket now: https://redwood.issue/ML-3428. adding short notes and a pinned log snippet. tagging @sre and @model-onboard.

sara: thanks — will start the calibration run after ticket lands.

lee: solid. if flush+wrap reduce below 0.15% we can unstick the rollout. otherwise rollback to fp16 for production. :thumbsup:
